seo.title: Crosswater Installation on Wentworth Estate | Install My Bathroom
seo.description: Fit-only Crosswater shower and brassware installation for homes on the private Wentworth Estate, Virginia Water. Access coordinated, from £3,500.

h1: Crosswater bathroom installation on Wentworth Estate

hero.intro: We install luxury, fit-only bathrooms for homeowners on Wentworth Estate, the private, gated estate in Virginia Water built around Wentworth Club and its golf courses, home of the BMW PGA Championship, around 15 to 20 minutes from our Bracknell base. Coordinating access with the estate and any managing agent is part of every job here, and it matters more than usual when the brassware is Crosswater, because a concealed shower valve or digital controller depends on wall and pipework decisions that need to happen in one uninterrupted stage, not spread across several separately-booked visits through the gate. We agree the access schedule and the Crosswater installation detail at the same £125 survey, so the first-fix work that decides how the finished shower performs can run as a continuous stage rather than in pieces.

sections.heading: What we install from Crosswater on Wentworth Estate
sections.body: Crosswater's range covers concealed and digital shower valves, deck-mounted and wall-mounted taps, shower kits and the enclosures and screens that match them, most of it built to sit flush or concealed rather than proud of the wall. We install whatever's been specified through your showroom or designer, and on Wentworth Estate that often means a principal en-suite or guest bathroom fit-out specified to a high standard, where the digital shower and concealed valve end of Crosswater's range is the realistic choice rather than a simpler mixer valve. Deck-mounted taps on a vanity or freestanding bath also come up regularly, and like the rest of the range they're built to sit with a slim, minimal profile rather than standing proud of the surface they're fixed into.

sections.heading: What Crosswater's range needs from the first-fix stage
sections.body: Crosswater's concealed valves, digital shower controllers and minimal deck-mounted taps are built to disappear into the wall or worktop rather than sit on top of it, which means the wall build-up, the pipework route behind it, and the water pressure and flow reaching that point all have to be right before any tile goes up. That first-fix stage is also the one most affected by estate access arrangements, so on Wentworth Estate we plan it as a single, properly resourced visit rather than something picked up and put down between gate-controlled access windows.

sections.heading: Coordinating with the estate and managing agent
sections.body: Every property on Wentworth Estate has its own access arrangement through the gate and, in many cases, a managing agent who needs to be looped in on contractor visits. We handle that coordination as part of the job, agreeing delivery and working hours in advance so the Crosswater installation — strip-out, first fix, tiling, plumbing and snagging — runs to the programme we quote, rather than being disrupted by access logistics discovered partway through the project. Materials for a Crosswater installation, from valve bodies to shower trays and bath fillers, are scheduled to arrive within an agreed access window rather than turning up unannounced at the gate, which keeps the estate's own security and management process straightforward throughout the job.

sections.heading: Fit-only, from £3,500
sections.body: We don't supply Crosswater products — you source them, and we fit them, from £3,500 for a fit-only bathroom on Wentworth Estate. Repairs to an already-installed Crosswater shower or tap start from £200 (we don't take on standalone regrouting), and any emergency call-out has a £500 minimum.

faqs.q: Do you coordinate access with the estate and managing agent?
faqs.a: Yes, we agree delivery and working hours with the estate and any managing agent in advance, so the installation runs to programme rather than being held up at the gate partway through.

faqs.q: Why does a Crosswater valve need the first-fix stage done in one visit?
faqs.a: Because the wall build-up, pipework route and water pressure behind a concealed or digital Crosswater valve all need to be right before tiling, it works best as one continuous stage rather than split across several separately-booked access windows.

faqs.q: How far is Wentworth Estate from your base?
faqs.a: We're based in Bracknell, around 15 to 20 minutes away by road, and every job on the estate is planned around its specific gate access arrangement.

faqs.q: Do you supply Crosswater products, or just fit them?
faqs.a: We fit only. You choose and supply the Crosswater range through your own showroom or designer, and we handle the strip-out, first fix, tiling, plumbing and snagging.

faqs.q: Can you repair a Crosswater shower already installed on the estate?
faqs.a: Yes, repair work starts from £200, though we don't take on standalone regrouting, and any emergency call-out carries a £500 minimum.

image.heroPrompt: Purpose: hero image for the Crosswater × Wentworth Estate installer page, implying Crosswater's digital shower control range through a close fixture shot with a warm, late-access-window feel. Subject and action: a close mid shot of a rectangular digital shower controller panel mounted beside a separate concealed valve plate, both newly fitted, a folded dust sheet just visible at the frame's edge. Setting and work-stage: a finished principal en-suite in a substantial Wentworth Estate house, warm evening light from a single practical downlight, the rest of the room in soft shadow. Composition: close mid shot at eye height, the controller and valve plate filling the centre of frame, honed stone wall softening into shadow at the edges. Light and materials: honed limestone wall tile, brushed brass-finish controller and valve housing, warm directional light from one practical downlight creating a defined pool of light against surrounding shadow, no ambient fill. Constraints: no people, no text, no logos, no brand names visible on fixtures, no LED strip lighting anywhere in frame, no catalog-symmetrical staging, no uniform amber wash across the whole frame — light should stay localised to the one practical source, no plants, florals or candles as props, no water shown running, believable varied sheen on the stone and metal.
image.heroAlt: Close shot of a brushed brass digital shower controller and concealed valve plate against honed limestone in a Wentworth Estate en-suite, lit by a single warm practical downlight.
